report.source_text: One year later there have been no further generalised seizures, but she reported occasional myoclonus, predominantly right sided, which worsens after exercise. Her jerks increased after reducing levetiracetam, which was reinstated. She has developed bilateral ptosis without ophthalmoplegia, with a right hemiparesis and a high-stepping gait.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Biallelic compound heterozygous POLG-related mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome (Alpers-Huttenlocher syndrome phenotype)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 21-year-old woman at 18 weeks gestation presented with new-onset focal impaired awareness seizures progressing to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures without preceding febrile illness. Initial MRI (E004) demonstrated new abnormal cortical signal involving the left parietal, posterolateral temporal and occipital lobes. She rapidly deteriorated into prolonged refractory status epilepticus requiring ICU admission, intubation, multiple anti-seizure medications, and intravenous corticosteroids (E001). Following surgical termination of pregnancy and extubation, she developed epilepsia partialis continua with continuous repetitive discharges over the left posterior region on EEG (E006). Clinical suspicion for POLG-related mitochondrial disease emerged during hospitalization, prompting withdrawal of valproate due to concern for hepatotoxicity, and lacosamide was added as a fifth agent (E006). Subsequent genetic testing confirmed biallelic compound heterozygous pathogenic POLG variants (c.2243G>C p.Trp748Ser and c.3720G>C). One-year follow-up (E010) revealed no further generalized seizures but persistent right-sided myoclonus exacerbated by exercise and medication reduction, along with new neurological deficits including bilateral ptosis, right hemiparesis, and high-stepping gait, consistent with progressive mitochondrial disease.
